verdict.rationale: Alacritty documents official support for Linux, macOS, Windows and BSD, with package-manager installs and prebuilt binaries, and it uses a single TOML config file format that supports imports. However, a 2026 runtime probe found the macOS Homebrew cask disabled because the published binaries fail Gatekeeper, so macOS currently means building from source or bypassing Gatekeeper. A Windows user also hit TOML config gotchas and shortcuts that would not work. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that one config file is portable unchanged across all three OSes, a working signed macOS binary or installer, and hands-on corroboration of identical behavior on each platform.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the same terminal with the same config on macOS, Linux, and Windows

citations.quote: The supported platforms currently consist of BSD, Linux, macOS and Windows.
Alacritty can be installed by using various package managers on Linux, BSD, macOS and Windows.
Alacritty's configuration file uses the TOML format.
Imports are loaded in order, skipping all missing files, with the importing file being loaded last.
